The warehouse associate was picking bar stock from the third level of the material rack in the stores area. The task was underway because the bar stock was on a pick list for a machining job due that afternoon. Stage of the task: transport, moving or handling material. Method in effect: SW-077 Material Rack Picking. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Material rack MR-11 in the stores area, third level. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped and loaded or under tension. Equipment condition: The rack has no end stops fitted on the third level, which was noted at the last rack inspection. Object handled weighed approximately 30 pounds for the length that fell. Object size and shape: a 6 foot length of 2 inch round bar stock. The object was held as follows: the adjacent length was being drawn out with both hands at about chest height. PPE in use: Safety glasses, steel toe boots and cut resistant gloves, no hard hat. This matched the PPE specified for the task. Immediately before the event: standing square to the rack at the third level with both hands on a length of bar stock at about chest height, drawing it toward the body. At the moment of the event: the adjacent length rolled sideways as the first was withdrawn, travelled off the open end of the rack, and fell onto the left shoulder from the level above. Immediately after the event: the bar landed on the floor, the associate stepped back from the rack holding the left shoulder, and a coworker at the next aisle called the supervisor. The warehouse associate was struck by a moving object. Mechanism: A 6 foot length of steel bar stock rolled off the open end of the third rack level and fell onto the left shoulder, which was stationary. Direction and distance of travel: from above and slightly behind, falling about 2 feet from the level above. Mass or speed of the object: approximately 30 pounds, falling freely. Point of contact and direction of force: the top of the left shoulder, struck from directly above with the force directed downward. Difference from a normal run of this task: The third level had been loaded with mixed lengths that morning rather than the usual single size, so the lengths did not sit tight against each other. Conditions at the point of injury: poor or glaring lighting. Detail: The stores aisle is lit from the main bay and the upper rack levels sit in shadow, so a loose length is hard to see from below. Timing: About 4 hours into an 8 hour shift and roughly 2 minutes into this pick. The warehouse associate had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: The missing end stops on rack MR-11 were raised at the last rack inspection and the corrective action to fit them is still open. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: End stops are the specified control for preventing material rolling off the rack and none are fitted on the third level. Stop-work opportunity: The pick could have been stopped once the mixed lengths were seen, but loading mixed lengths is common and was not treated as a hazard. First aid at the scene: A cold pack was applied to the left shoulder in the first aid room for about 20 minutes. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notification: The supervisor attended within about two minutes and EHS within fifteen minutes. Scene and equipment: The aisle was barriered and the rack level was unloaded before picking resumed. Work at the location stopped. The warehouse associate was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
